# Contest contract

This six-problem contest mixes Sections 70--71. All statements are local and
self-contained. The order is progressive, but later tasks deliberately hide
the reduction behind assignment, graph, or resource language.

| Problem | Main compression |
|---|---|
| A | lower bounds become vertex imbalances |
| B | reduced costs and potential-based shortest paths |
| C | lower-quota slots plus min-cost assignment |
| D | convex derivative stored as heap breakpoints |
| E | Lagrangian price for an exact color count |
| F | quota flow plus convex marginal-cost edges |

# Suggested contest use

Allow four hours. Before coding, write one sentence naming the conserved
quantity or ordered marginal structure. For E and F, also write how ties or
the forcing constant are certified. Upsolve every task with a tiny brute-force
oracle; these techniques are especially vulnerable to plausible but false
binary-search conditions.

# Reduction triage

Before building a graph or writing a heap, isolate which part of the statement
is difficult.

| Difficult phrase | First transformation to investigate |
|---|---|
| every choice has a minimum and maximum usage | subtract lower bounds |
| exactly `F` indistinguishable units, additive edge costs | min-cost flow |
| one worker chooses one eligible project | bipartite unit flow |
| later units become progressively more expensive | marginal-cost expansion |
| an exact count breaks an otherwise easy optimizer | Lagrangian price |
| values must be monotone under absolute loss | convex derivative / slope trick |

Several problems contain two rows of this table. Apply transformations one at
a time and preserve their proof obligations. For example, F first turns
quadratic congestion into ordered marginal slots, then embeds those slots in a
quota-constrained assignment flow.

# How to find A: conservation before optimization

Ignore all costs because A has none. Exact group demand means fixed flow out
of the source; room minima and maxima are bounded edges to the sink. The
allowed group-room pairs form the only unit middle edges. A fixed return edge
closes the network into a circulation.

The important reasoning is bidirectional. A valid seating selection sends one
unit along every chosen pair. Conversely, integrality makes every used middle
edge a discrete selected pair. Without this second direction, a network may
silently admit fractional or repeated choices that the statement forbids.

# How to find E: price the one awkward statistic

Without the exact number of discounted edges, E is simply an MST. This tells
us what not to replace: keep Kruskal and move only the exact count into the
objective. Adding `lambda` per discounted edge creates a family of ordinary
MST instances.

The binary-search predicate is not “the returned tree has exactly `k`.” At a
tie, equally optimal trees can have different counts. The correct observation
is an interval: red-first and blue-first Kruskal give the maximum and minimum
counts among modified-optimal trees. The target is feasible at that price when
it lies between them.

# How to find F: expose discrete derivatives

A team used `x` times pays `a*x^2`. Compute consecutive differences:

```text
cost(x) - cost(x-1) = a*(2x-1).
```

These marginals are nondecreasing, so a minimum-cost flow using `x` team slots
will take the first `x`. The nonlinear objective has become ordinary parallel
unit edges. This “differentiate a discrete convex cost” move is useful whenever
the total cost is separable by resource.

# Proof map

For A--C and F, use three layers:

1. prove the original objects and integral flows correspond;
2. prove capacities, bounds, or rewarded slots encode feasibility exactly;
3. prove the residual algorithm optimizes cost among feasible flows.

For D, name the convex prefix value function and the meaning of every stored
breakpoint. For E, prove monotonicity with respect to the price and prove tie
interval attainability. A binary search without both facts is only an
experiment.

# C++ and Python reliability

- Use 64-bit capacities only when the total flow can exceed `int`.
- Use 128-bit arithmetic for `BIG`, quadratic marginal sums, and penalized MST
  values when the product bounds require it.
- In Python, heap records and residual edges dominate memory; avoid one object
  wrapper per tiny record.
- Update potentials only for vertices reached by Dijkstra.
- Check saturation of every lexicographically rewarded lower-quota slot rather
  than assuming a large constant worked.

# Stress-oracle design

For tiny instances, enumerate subsets for A, all integral path flows for B,
worker assignments for C and F, bounded repaired sequences for D, and spanning
trees for E. The oracle should implement the statement directly. Reusing the
same reduction as the optimized solution confirms only that both programs made
the same modeling mistake.

Useful adversarial families include equal-cost routes, tight lower bounds,
disconnected eligibility graphs, many equal modified MST weights, and several
marginals equal to the threshold.

# Exercises

Solve A--F as one contest. The mixed set contains exactly six new local
problems and covers every principal invariant introduced in Sections 70--71.
